items.content:
I sometimes wonder why we Indian IT professionals define success mostly by money.

“I went from 4 LPA → 20 LPA.”
“Company X pays this much.”
“This role has a 50% hike.”

But I rarely see people say:

“I started with this skillset, learned these things, and now I can solve these problems and bring this much value to my team.”

Money is definitely a good motivation. It gives us freedom, security and a better life.

But somewhere, we turned it into a rat race. And I sometimes wonder if we are also slowly spoiling our work culture because of it.

People start chasing packages, titles and switches instead of skills, ownership, learning and the problems they actually enjoy solving.

Maybe instead of always asking “How much are you earning?”, we should also ask:

“What can you do today that you couldn’t do 5 years ago?”

Money ≠ Passion.
Money ≠ Mastery.
Money ≠ Success.

They can go together, but they are not the same thing.

items.content:
RT @dwarkesh_sp: Had @RyanGreenblatt on to discuss/debate recursive self-improvement.

This might be the most important question in the world right now - whether within a year or so of achieving human level intelligence, you slingshot towards having 10s of billions of superintelligences, each of which is dramatically more competent than human experts across all fields.

I’ve historically been skeptical of this possibility. My intuition has been that we will end up significantly bottlenecked by not only compute scaling but human expert data, which I think underlies most of the AI progress today.

If, because of RSI, we got a jump as big as GPT-3 to a Mythos (i.e. 6 years of AI progress) within a single year of achieving AGI, then the thing we get there at the end of that year is definitively and wildly superhuman.

We hashed it out, and I think Ryan made a pretty good case that this kind of speedup is plausible. FWIW, Ryan’s median for when we automate AI R&D is 2031.

We then discussed the alignment implications of this scenario. Who should these superintelligences be aligned to? In the future, our capacity to steward our votes and our capital, and to make sense of what's happening in the world, will all be titrated by superintelligences. And I worry that specs like the Claude Constitution are not shaping these ASIs to truly be my personal advocates and guardian angels.

And can we get them aligned to anything in the first place? Ryan and I had a long debate about whether the kind of reward hacking we saw with the OAI/Hugging Face hack extrapolates to superintelligences that would team up to literally take over the world.

The first piece of advice you get when you're learning to drive is that it will go much smoother if you look at the horizon instead of directly in front of your tires. And so it is with the trajectory of AI. Hope you enjoy!

0:00:00 – Is AI R&D verifiable enough to unlock recursive self-improvement?
0:16:52 – Is AI progress bottlenecked by human expert data?
0:34:02 – Flat token prices suggest scaling has been slow
0:39:47 – Skills AI can't train on: does it even need them?
0:48:07 – Aligned to whom?
1:09:18 – Recent incidents of AIs colluding and deceiving humans
1:19:38 – What could possibly go wrong? A concrete scenario
1:48:02 – From reward hacking to takeover

items.content:
DPRK's OtterCookie variant uses different ports for different jobs: 8086 for primary file exfiltration, 8085 for secondary file exfiltration, and 8087 for Socket[.]IO C2, clipboard, and log exfiltration.

That makes its infrastructure surprisingly easy to hunt. With a simple Censys query matching all three ports, Express, and the same hosting provider, we can identify C2 infrastructure that appears to be still active or recently configured.

Long live @censysio 

Censys Query:
```
https://t.co/AsIwcplBKC.port = "8085" and https://t.co/AsIwcplBKC.port = "8086" and https://t.co/AsIwcplBKC.port = "8087" and https://t.co/R9wN1leYIr.vendor = "express" and host.autonomous_system.description = "ROUTERHOSTING - RouterHosting LLC"
```

Discovered C2 infrastructure:
```
144.172.117[.]220
153.75.89[.]4
167.88.167[.]54
104.194.134[.]213
```

items.content:
The addiction and hype around hacking, coding, reversing, research, gaming, and computers in general is very real. When passion turns into obsession, it can slowly come at the expense of your mental, physical, and social well-being.

And it is a really hard balance to strike, even if you are not constantly publishing research. There are plenty of people quietly spending huge amounts of time building projects, learning techniques, reversing things, experimenting, or doing solid research that may never be published, whether it is novel or not.

Sometimes the pressure comes from the work itself, not from having an audience. When you genuinely enjoy something and constantly want to get better at it, knowing when to stop is difficult. The work will always be there, but your health and the people around you matter too.

🔗 Report: https://t.co/Vz351iWmcm

We found a sample likely written in Rust which drops Stealc and a malicious Chrome extension pretending to be GoogleTranslate. 

The extension can extract the browser history, bookmarks, a list of installed extensions, credentials, and cookies. It also provides threat actors with a live stream of Chrome windows and allows them to remotely control websites using mouse clicks and keyboard input. 

However, to hide those remote actions from the victim's view, the extension also allows remote control of out-of-focus windows in the background. 

Furthermore, the extension can overlay legitimate login forms with an iframe from a phishing page while keeping the legitimate domain visible in the address bar.

items.content:
RT @splinter_code: I noticed an interesting change starting from Windows 11 22H2 in the behavior of NtSystemDebugControl when taking a live kernel dump (SysDbgGetLiveKernelDump) including user-mode pages (flag IncludeUserSpaceMemoryPages).

Until Windows 11 21H2 code in nt!DbgkCaptureLiveKernelDump returned STATUS_DEBUGGER_INACTIVE when the IncludeUserSpaceMemoryPages flag was requested and the kernel debugger was not attached/configured.
Starting from Windows 11 22H2 a new feature named "LivedumpProcessFiltering" is checked and it basically skips that check allowing to take the dump including usermode pages regardless of the kernel debugger status.

This means that in newer Windows taking kernel dumps including sensitive information (e.g. lsass.exe memory) is easier and wouldn't require any reboot/boot changes to enable the kernel debugger nor relying on any external third-party drivers.

items.content:
RT @InsiderGeo: NEW: 🇸🇪 Sweden's Security Service (Säpo) says it has stopped a Russian intelligence operation in Stockholm involving the SVR, Russia's foreign intelligence service.

According to Säpo, two Russian intelligence officers recruited an agent working at another country's embassy in Sweden and maintained contact through meetings at restaurants and during walks around Stockholm.

Säpo says it was able to follow and map the operation for a long period, including monitoring meetings between the Russian officers and the recruited agent. Investigators say they observed not only the meetings, but also gifts being handed over to the agent.

The objective was to obtain information concerning central Swedish decision-making and use the recruited intermediary to potentially influence Swedish politics, particularly on polarizing issues. 

Säpo says it has a detailed picture of the assignments given to the agent and the questions the agent subsequently asked.

According to deputy operations chief Christoffer Wedelin, these activities were identified and ultimately interrupted by Säpo. He said the agency is making the case public because it provides a concrete example of what the Russian intelligence threat looks like in Sweden today.

The three individuals cannot be arrested or prosecuted because they were operating under diplomatic immunity. All three have now left Sweden.

Swedish Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer said the government considers the incident serious and described it as part of a broader pattern of Russia working strategically and over the long term to advance its interests in Sweden.
